battle.name: 始州之戰
battle.brief: 北周大象二年，益州人李嚴聚眾為亂、據成都，叛軍蔓延梁益二州。宣帝宇文邕以隨國公楊堅為行軍總管入蜀，兵鋒直指嘉陵江上游的州治始州，即今四川閬中。城頭弩砲壓住城下攻城者，援軍到位後反客為主，叛軍主力潰散，李嚴西走，蜀地重歸朝廷，亦為隋文帝代周建隋積下的一步。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 北周一方是中原的中央政權：皇帝周宣帝宇文邕坐鎮京師，下令討蜀，兵事由受命的統帥主持，楊堅以隨國公之號擔任行軍總管，節制從關中、漢中、劍州一線調來的宿衛與邊軍，後方是長安至洛陽的糧秣通道。蜀中李嚴一方並非外國，而是北周邊內的地方叛軍，以益州本地人為主體，聯絡梁、益二州的州縣吏員、地方豪右與巴蜀山中的僚、氐、羌等部眾，據成都、憑劍閣道與嘉陵江上游的險要立寨。整場衝突沒有第三國參與，也沒有正式同盟；陳朝只在江南一側遙相呼應，可能提供糧械與使者的接觸，諸說並存。北周的目標是收回益梁、恢復朝廷對蜀地的直接控制與賦稅，叛軍的目標則是據蜀自立、割據一方，把水陸要道握在手中。整體格局是北周滅齊之後、正當對陳用兵的前夜，蜀地恰好夾在兩大政權之間，任何一方的失手都可能被江南利用。
countriesEn: The Zhou side was a Central Plains dynasty: Emperor Xuan of Zhou, Yuwen Yong, sat at the capital and ordered the suppression, with the operation entrusted to a commander-in-chief, Yang Jian, who held the title of Duke of Sui and controlled the imperial guards and frontier troops drawn from Guanzhong, Hanzhong and the Jianzhou area, with the grain route running from Chang'an toward Luoyang. Li Yan's side was not a foreign power but a local rebellion inside Zhou's own borders, based mainly on natives of Yizhou and linked with the commandery officials of Liang and Yi prefectures, the local magnates, and the Liao, Di and Qiang groups of the Sichuan mountains; it occupied Chengdu and built strongholds along the Jianmen road and the upper Jialing. No third state took part and there was no formal alliance; the Chen court in the south could only respond at a distance, possibly offering supplies and envoys, and the details remain disputed. Zhou's aim was to recover Yi and Liang and restore direct imperial control and taxation over Sichuan, while the rebels' aim was to hold the province, stand on their own and keep the water and land routes in their hands. The wider frame is the years after Zhou destroyed Northern Qi and before the great campaign against Chen, with Sichuan lying between two rival courts, so a setback on either side could be exploited from the south.
people: 決定這場戰役走向的是三個人。北周宣帝宇文邕是下令的一方，他當時已滅北齊、正在籌劃大舉南伐，蜀地叛亂直接威脅到西南邊軍的徵調與軍糧，故命大將出征；他的決策帶有明顯的威懾意味，想以一次迅速平亂震懾內外。隋文帝楊堅——此時以隨國公出仕、握北周兵柄——是真正的統兵者，他自漢中、劍閣入蜀，兵鋒直抵嘉陵江上游的始州。楊堅之能，一半在於用兵果決，一半在於他從不把叛逆只當作敵人來打，屢次在軍中即時安撫州縣、收納歸附官吏，所以成都平定之後蜀地人心很快歸附，這一點對他日後掌北周、進而代周建隋影響深遠。第三人是被討伐的益州起事首領李嚴，據成都、擁眾自居，兵敗之後西走，餘部退入山區，其終局在諸史中只留數語。地方上，益梁二州的刺史、縣吏與豪右多在兩造之間觀望，陳朝一側的往來使者亦在史家的推測之列，具體經過諸說並存。後世《隋書·高祖紀》與《北史·周本紀》各以數語帶過此役，戰情細節多賴零星記載與地方志的補充。
peopleEn: Three men shaped the outcome. Yuwen Yong, Emperor Xuan of Zhou, issued the order: having already destroyed Northern Qi he was preparing a great southern campaign, and a revolt in Sichuan directly threatened the recruitment of southwestern troops and the military grain, so he sent a general to deal with it; the intent was openly deterrent, to end the revolt quickly and warn both inside and outside the empire. Yang Jian — then serving as Duke of Sui and holding military power in Zhou — was the man who actually led the army, marching into Shu from Hanzhong and Jianmen until his vanguard reached Shizhou on the upper Jialing. His strength lay half in decisiveness and half in never treating a rebellion as a mere enemy to be destroyed: he repeatedly pacified prefectures and accepted officials who submitted while the campaign was still in the field, and so after Chengdu fell the Sichuanese submitted quickly, a point that shaped his later control of Zhou and his usurpation of the dynasty. The third figure was Li Yan, the Yizhou insurgent who occupied Chengdu, whose defeat sent him westward while his remnants scattered into the mountains; his fate survives only in a few lines of the histories. Locally, the prefects, county magistrates and magnates of Yi and Liang waited to see which side would win, and Chen envoys appear in later speculation, with the exact course of events disputed. Later historians compressed the campaign into a few lines in the Annals of Emperor Gaozu of Sui and the Northern History, and the tactical detail survives only in scattered records and local gazetteers.
kits: 本卡的主兵器是秦弩，也就是中國式的弩。弩的關鍵在弩機：張弦時把拉力蓄在機括之中，扣發只需一下小小的扳動，因此不必像弓那樣靠臂力持續拉滿，受傷或疲乏的射手仍可繼續射擊；野外行軍與守城時，弩手可以伏在牆垛後或土壘後方，穩定地向數十步至百步外齊射，而無須站起來與敵人對拉。出土的漢代弩機多帶銅製機括與鍵栓，可見這項技術在漢代已相當成熟，兩漢以降的邊軍與郡國兵都把它列為常備裝備。南北朝時的軍隊通常把弩手與長兵手混編在同一支隊伍裡，弩手先以密集的矢雨覆蓋敵陣與攻城器械，步騎再趁隙衝擊；守城一方更倚重弩，居高臨下地壓住城下的進攻者，使雲梯、撞車無法貼近牆根。北周軍入蜀時除攜帶通用弩機，還調有床弩一類的重型射具，專門對付城牆與船隻。與弩配合的還有鎧甲、步槍、長刀、戟、弓，以及投石、撞車、拒馬、鹿角等攻守器具；蜀地山道狹窄，馬匹有限，糧秣多賴嘉陵江水運與人力挑運，劍閣棧道只能通行小隊與輜重。
kitsEn: The featured weapon is the Chinese crossbow. Its heart is the lock mechanism: the pull is stored in the trigger assembly when the string is drawn, and releasing it costs only a small squeeze of the lever, so the archer does not have to hold a bow at full draw and can keep shooting even when tired or wounded. In the field and on the walls, crossbowmen could lie behind crenellations or earthen works and deliver steady volleys at ranges of several dozen to a hundred paces without standing up to pull against the enemy. Han-dynasty lock mechanisms excavated in the south and in Sichuan were cast in bronze, showing how mature the technique already was in that era, and the border armies and commandery troops of the later Han and the period of division all treated the crossbow as standard equipment. Southern and Northern Dynasties armies normally intermingled crossbowmen with men of the longer weapons, the crossbowmen opening with dense arrow-falls that covered the enemy formation and their siege machines before infantry and cavalry struck through the gap; a defending side leaned on the crossbow even more, holding the attackers down from above so that ladders and battering rams could not reach the wall base. Beyond the standard crossbow locks, the Zhou troops marching into Shu brought heavier devices such as bed crossbows, meant for walls and ships, together with armour, spears, long swords, halberds, bows, and stone-throwers, battering rams, caltrops and deer-horn barricades. Narrow mountain tracks limited the use of horses in Shu, grain moved chiefly by barge on the Jialing and by human porters, and the Jianmen plank road carried only small columns and baggage trains.
tactics: 北周軍入蜀的路線決定了整場戰役的樣貌。從關中出兵，過漢中、越劍門是一條最直接的路，但劍閣棧道只容單隊通行，難以展開人數，因此統軍者把主力沿白水河與嘉陵江谷地分批推進，讓前隊出劍閣作前鋒、主力由水路上行，形成夾在山道與河道之間的縱隊。始州是這條線上的關鍵：它當著嘉陵江上游的門戶，北倚劍閣道南口，南控通往成都的水路，州城一旦失守，叛軍便可據江而守、截斷援軍的糧道。叛軍主力圍攻始州、企圖先拔這顆釘子，攻城卻遭到城頭弩的壓制，雲梯難以接近，屢攻不下。援軍抵達之後並不急於強攻，而是先以弩手列陣，齊射覆蓋城下與山坡上的叛軍陣地及攻城器械，再以步騎出城反擊，把叛軍擠離城牆；退入山地的叛眾又被截斷糧道，首腦西走，部眾星散。善後階段，朝廷的處置並非一律誅戮：據說有照舊留任歸附官吏、免除重役、就地徵糧一類的寬恤做法，具體細節史無明文，諸說並存；可以確定的是大軍並未深入叢林，而蜀地也因此很快安定下來。
tacticsEn: The route the Zhou army took into Shu shaped the whole campaign. Leaving Guanzhong, crossing Hanzhong and passing Jianmen was the most direct line, but the Jianmen plank road admitted single files only and could not deploy a large force, so the commander pushed the main body in batches along the valleys of the Baishui and the Jialing, with an advance element coming through Jianmen and the main body moving up by water, the column thus strung out between the mountain track and the river. Shizhou was the hinge of that line: it commanded the upper Jialing, with Jianmen and the southern mouth of the plank road behind it and the road to Chengdu below, and once it fell the rebels could hold the river and cut the grain route of the relieving army. The rebel main body besieged Shizhou in order to pull this nail out first, but the siege was pinned by the crossbows on the walls, whose volleys kept the ladders from closing, and no assault carried. When the relief force arrived it did not strike at once: it first deployed the crossbowmen in line, whose volleys covered the rebel positions at the foot of the wall and on the slopes together with their siege machines, and then sent infantry and cavalry out of the city to drive the rebels away from the walls; the rebels who withdrew into the mountains had their grain route cut, their leaders fled west and their numbers scattered. In the aftermath the court did not simply execute everyone: according to the accounts, officials who submitted were left in office, the corvée was remitted and grain was requisitioned locally, though the details are not set down in the histories and the versions differ. What is certain is that the army did not march deep into the forest, which is why Sichuan settled so quickly.
data: 能夠核實的數字有限，先列可用的：始州即今四川閬中，在嘉陵江上游北岸，位於北緯三十一度附近、東經一百零六度上下；由劍門關到始州，沿山道約三百公里上下，谷地行軍往往比里程更慢；由始州順嘉陵江、涪江而下至成都，水程約三百至四百公里。兵員方面，現存史籍沒有留下確切的編制數字，只以概略的說法帶過：有記載稱叛軍有數萬之眾，但分部、名籍與糧秣總數都已無從復原；北周方面出動的是行軍總管直轄的精銳宿衛與漢中、劍州邊軍組成的混成部隊，規模同樣只能從親征大軍一類的定性描述推想。裝備數據中較可靠的一項是弩的張力：漢代弩機與蹶張弩的張力在百公斤一級，臨陣射速可數倍於拉弓。時間上，起事與開戰的確切月份在史書中無從考定，本卡暫繫於秋季；自入蜀到成都平定，所歷時間在諸史中同樣只用概略的字眼帶過。糧秣方面，劍閣棧道每日僅能通行有限數量的輜重，多數糧食靠嘉陵江轉運，軍隊初期的推進速度因此受制於水情。
dataEn: Few figures can be verified. Shizhou is present-day Langzhong in Sichuan, on the north bank of the upper Jialing, at roughly thirty-one degrees north and one hundred and six degrees east; the mountain road from Jianmen Gate to Shizhou runs to about three hundred kilometres, though marching through the valleys is slower than the mileage suggests, and the water route down the Jialing and the Fu to Chengdu is roughly three hundred to four hundred kilometres. On numbers of troops the surviving records leave no exact establishment, only general statements: some accounts give the rebels tens of thousands, but their organisation, muster rolls and grain totals cannot be recovered, and the Zhou force was a mixed body of picked imperial guards and frontier troops from Hanzhong and Jianzhou under the commander's own hand, its size being inferable only from such characterisations as a personally led main army. The more reliable equipment figure concerns the crossbow: Han lock mechanisms and the pedal crossbow reached a draw weight on the order of a hundred kilograms, and their rate of fire in the line was several times that of the bow. In time, no month is recorded for the rising or the opening of the campaign, and the card is provisionally placed in the autumn; the span from the march into Shu to the reduction of Chengdu is likewise given only in general terms. On supply, the plank road could carry only a limited volume of baggage a day, so most grain came by barge on the Jialing, and the speed of the advance in the early stages was governed by the state of the water.
cause: 起事的前提，是北周對蜀地的治理一直存在裂縫。蜀中自十六國以來歷經前趙、前蜀、後蜀等割據政權，州郡豪右與中央的關係一向微妙；北周滅北齊、接管巴蜀之後，益州的賦役、徵發與軍隊調度仍多倚賴地方勢力，朝廷派出的刺史與軍鎮彼此牽制，一遇災荒或上命過苛，怨氣便會匯聚到一點。外部環境同樣重要：北周主力在北邊與陳朝對峙，一旦益州失控，江南便可利用蜀道把兵員與物資輸送到關中背後，這是宣帝不能容忍的。就在大象初年，益州一帶的地方官員因處置失當、豪右彼此傾軋而激出變亂，李嚴乘勢聚眾，據成都、聯絡梁州與山中的部眾，蜀中數郡先後響應。這場起事的直接導火線在現存記載中並不清晰，《隋書》《北史》都只用數語帶過，起義的宗教口號、組織章程與對陳朝求援的具體經過皆無明文，諸說並存；可以確定的只是，蜀地長期積累的治理矛盾遇上北周對外用兵、內部多事的一個空檔，造就了這場叛亂。至於李嚴本人的出身與年歲，諸史亦載之不詳。
causeEn: The uprising presupposed a long fracture in Zhou's government of Shu. Since the Sixteen Kingdoms the region had passed through Former Zhao, Former Shu and Later Shu, and the relation between the great families of the prefectures and the centre had always been delicate; after Zhou destroyed Northern Qi and took over Bashu, the taxes, levies and troop transfers in Yizhou still relied heavily on local power, and the governors and military commands appointed by the court checked one another, so that a bad harvest or an overbearing order could concentrate the resentment. The external setting mattered as much: Zhou's main strength was tied down opposite Chen, and once Yizhou slipped out of control the south could use the Shu roads to move men and materiel behind Guanzhong, which the emperor could not tolerate. In the early Dàxiàng years, mishandling by local officials and quarrels among the great families set off the disturbance, and Li Yan seized the moment, gathering followers, occupying Chengdu and drawing in Liangzhou and the mountain groups, several prefectures of Shu answering in turn. The immediate spark is not clear in the surviving record, since the Sui and Northern Histories compress the whole affair into a few lines, and the religious slogans, the organisation and the precise channels of appeal to Chen are all unrecorded, with the versions differing. What can be asserted is that the accumulated contradictions of rule in Shu coincided with a moment when Zhou was committed abroad and beset by trouble at home, and that this produced the revolt. As for Li Yan's own origins and age, the histories do not say.
impact: 此役的後果分成兩層。眼前一層是蜀地的平定：始州與益州、梁州一線重歸北周朝廷的直接控制，叛軍殘部退入山區後被地方軍鎮次第清剿，若干年內不再成為大規模的邊患，而北周在西南的兵源與糧源從此可以就近徵發，不必再仰賴關中長途運補。深一層的影響落在楊堅身上：始州之戰是他以行軍總管身份獨當一面、迅速平定邊亂的又一個功績，關中與河北的朝野由此更認定他有將才與柄力，這份威望在宣帝病逝、靜帝幼弱之後迅速轉化為權力；同年之後不數年，北周為隋所代，楊堅即皇帝位。對南面的陳朝而言，蜀地歸北周等於失去一條向西北伸出的手臂，長江上游的西面再無可供轉圜的支點，而蜀道的北口與南口都掌握在隋的手中，日後隋軍東下滅陳、其後經略吐谷渾與梁州，都以此為基地。兵制與技術上，弩在西南山地攻防中的地位再次被確認：守城以弩壓制坡下進攻、行軍以弩手掩護縱隊前進，後世兵書把這套以弩當壁的守城之法列為西南戰守的常規，而此役正是這類經驗在正史中少數留下名字的實例。
impactEn: The consequences fall into two layers. In the immediate layer, Shu was pacified: Shizhou and the line of the Yi and Liang prefectures returned to direct imperial control, the surviving rebels were chased into the mountains and were cleared away piece by piece by the regional garrisons, and for some years the province no longer troubled the empire as a major frontier risk, while Zhou could henceforth draw its southwestern men and grain on the spot instead of hauling everything over long distances from Guanzhong. The deeper effect fell on Yang Jian: Shizhou was another instance of his assuming sole command of a frontier command and settling a rebellion quickly, and the court and the northern provinces came to regard him all the more as a man of military talent and political weight. That standing turned into power once the emperor fell ill and the child emperor succeeded him, and within a few years Zhou gave way to Sui, with Yang Jian taking the imperial title. For the Chen court in the south, the return of Shu to Zhou meant the loss of an arm reaching out to the northwest; the western end of the upper Yangtze offered no further pivot, and both the northern and southern gates of the Shu road were in Sui hands, so that the later campaigns down the Yangtze, and after them the operations against Tuyuhun and Liangzhou, all drew on this base. In military technique the campaign confirmed the standing of the crossbow in the defensive fighting of the southwestern mountains: holding the enemy below the slope from the walls with crossbow fire, and covering the moving column with crossbowmen on the march. Later military manuals set down this art of holding the wall with the crossbow as a standard measure for guarding the southwest, and this campaign is one of the few instances in the official histories where such experience carries a name.
result: 打到最後，始州城下的叛軍主力被壓垮，圍城的雲梯與器械在弩火覆蓋下失去作用，兵眾退散，首領李嚴西走，餘眾或散入山林，或隨之而去，益梁二州的城池與編戶重新歸入朝廷版籍。朝廷沒有對蜀地作大規模的懲罰性改造，歸附的州縣官吏多照舊留任，百姓的賦役獲得寬減，因此表面上的平定很快轉成實質的歸附，這一點在史家的評價中被視為楊堅用兵不專恃力的一面。殘餘的叛眾在山區零星抵抗，斷續數年，直到地方軍鎮完成清剿才算收束。整體而言，北周用一次規模不大而時機恰當的用兵，保住了西南邊防，也讓楊堅在通往皇位的路上再行一步。至於此役的具體斬獲、俘虜、耗糧數字，正史皆未記載，只有《隋書》《北史》數語概括為蜀平；連同起事月份、李嚴下落等細節，學界至今仍多作保留，諸說並存。
resultEn: At the end, the rebel main body was broken below the walls of Shizhou: their ladders and siege machines lost all use under the covering volleys, the troops scattered, the leader Li Yan fled west, and either the remainder dispersed into the mountains or followed him, the cities and registered households of Yi and Liang once more returning to the imperial registers. The court did not impose a sweeping punitive reconstruction on Shu, and officials who submitted were mostly left in office while the burdens on the people were reduced, so a surface pacification quickly became real submission, a point later historians read as the side of Yang Jian's generalship that did not rest on force alone. Rebel remnants kept up an intermittent resistance in the hills for several years until the regional garrisons had finished clearing them out. In overall terms, the campaign was a modest but well-timed use of force that preserved the southwest frontier and gave Yang Jian one more step on the road to the throne. As for the specific numbers of enemy killed, prisoners taken and grain consumed, the official histories record none, reducing the affair to a few lines saying that Shu was pacified; and details such as the month of the rising and Li Yan's ultimate fate remain matters of reserve for scholars, with the versions differing.
